candidates.angle: smoke veils fire, so flaws veil all action
kunteya, son of kunti, is a name for arjuna
even flawed action must not be abandoned
candidates.evidence: सदोषमपि न त्यजेत् (do not abandon even with fault)

angle_en: Smoke veils fire, so flaws veil all action
angle_hi: धुआं आग को ढकता है, वैसे ही दोष हर कर्म को ढकते हैं

en.intro: Before you leave a task because it feels imperfect, listen to how Krishna explains why no action is ever perfect.
en.notice: Krishna says all undertakings are clouded by some defect, just as fire is veiled by smoke. The smoke does not mean the fire is gone; it means the fire is hidden, and you must still do your natural duty.
en.meaning: O son of Kunti, one should not abandon one's natural duty, even if it has flaws. All undertakings are clouded by some defect, just as fire is veiled by smoke.

hi.intro: कोई काम इसलिए न छोड़ें कि उसमें कमी है, कुरुक्षेत्र के इस वचन में कृष्ण समझाते हैं कि कोई भी कर्म दोषरहित नहीं होता।
hi.meaning: हे कुन्तीनन्दन दोषयुक्त होनेपर भी सहज कर्मका त्याग नहीं करना चाहिये क्योंकि सम्पूर्ण कर्म धुएँसे अग्निकी तरह किसीनकिसी दोषसे युक्त हैं ॥

en.intro: Before you leave a task because it feels imperfect, listen to how Krishna explains why no action is ever perfect.
en.body: O son of Kunti, one should not abandon one's natural duty, even if it has flaws. All undertakings are clouded by some defect, just as fire is veiled by smoke. Krishna says all undertakings are clouded by some defect, just as fire is veiled by smoke. The smoke does not mean the fire is gone; it means the fire is hidden, and you must still do your natural duty. Next, Krishna continues.

hi.body: हे कुन्तीनन्दन दोषयुक्त होनेपर भी सहज कर्मका त्याग नहीं करना चाहिये क्योंकि सम्पूर्ण कर्म धुएँसे अग्निकी तरह किसीनकिसी दोषसे युक्त हैं ॥ आगे श्रीकृष्ण कहते हैं।

issues: meaning_changed: "सच्ची निष्ठा का उच्चतम स्तर त्याग से नहीं, बल्कि अपने मन पर विजय पाने से आता है" (This phrase in the Hindi 'next' section misrepresents verse 49. The source states that one attains the highest perfection of non-action through renunciation (tyaga), not that it comes from mastering the self instead of renunciation. The script inverts the core message of the next verse.)

contrast_template: "न कि" (The Hindi 'notice' uses the contrast 'न कि' ('not that... but') to frame the relationship between the fire and the smoke, which is not present in the source. The source states they are analogous ('just as fire is veiled by smoke'), not that one is being negated in favor of the other.)
